skill.name: recoup-platform-email-helper
skill.description: Sends validated plain-text or HTML email through the Recoup API using a dependency-free Node helper with previews and explicit failure handling.
skill.summary: Send serialized Recoup emails with body validation, previews, and clear delivery errors.
skill.author: recoupable

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, comments, and JavaScript template literals. The review confirms outbound email delivery, sensitive credential use, unrestricted local file reads, and an environment-configurable authenticated endpoint. Predictable temporary paths in the documentation also create integrity risk.

remediation.issue: An environment-controlled API base receives the bearer credential and message content.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and allowlist trusted Recoup hosts before adding the Authorization header. Reject credentials for every unapproved destination.

remediation.issue: Caller-selected files can become outbound email content without path restrictions.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict file inputs to approved workspace paths and require explicit confirmation before sending file-derived content to external recipients.

remediation.issue: The documented workflow uses a predictable shared temporary filename.
remediation.suggestion: Use a securely created unique temporary file, set restrictive permissions, and remove it after the send attempt.

content.user_title: Send Reliable Emails Through the Recoup API
content.value_statement: Shell-built email payloads can break quoting and deliver empty messages. This helper validates content, serializes it safely, previews requests, and reports delivery failures.
actual_capabilities: Sends plain-text or HTML email through the Recoup API.
Reads message bodies from command arguments or local files.
Supports repeated recipient and carbon-copy addresses.
Adds an optional chat identifier for the email footer link.
Provides a dry-run preview without making the network request.
Rejects empty messages and reports network or API failures.
limitations: Requires Node 22 with global fetch support.
Requires a Recoup API key or access token for live sending.
Does not create attachments, templates, scheduling, or delivery analytics.
Does not validate recipient addresses or restrict file paths.

use_cases.title: Send an Account Report
use_cases.description: Deliver a generated HTML performance report to the account owner after previewing the serialized message.

use_cases.title: Notify an Operations Team
use_cases.description: Send a plain-text task result to several recipients and include relevant carbon-copy contacts.

use_cases.title: Deliver Workflow Alerts
use_cases.description: Add dependable email delivery to automated tasks with explicit exit codes and API error output.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Simple Email
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a plain-text email with subject [subject] and body [body]. Use dry-run mode and show the preview without sending.

prompt_templates.title: Send an HTML Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an HTML report from [report details], save it to a secure temporary file, preview it, then send it to [recipient].

prompt_templates.title: Notify Multiple Recipients
prompt_templates.prompt: Send [message] to [recipients], carbon copy [contacts], and include chat identifier [chat ID]. Confirm the final recipient list before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Verified Delivery Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate [report], preview the exact payload, verify the approved Recoup endpoint and recipients, send it, then report the message identifier or failure.

output_examples.input: Preview a weekly report email for the account owner.
output_examples.output: Dry run prepared for the Recoup email endpoint. Subject: Weekly Report. The validated HTML body is present, and no message was sent.

output_examples.input: Send the completed campaign summary to the approved recipient.
output_examples.output: The campaign summary was sent successfully. The service returned message identifier email_4821.

output_examples.input: Send a notification without a message body.
output_examples.output: The email was not sent because a non-empty HTML or plain-text body is required.

best_practices: Use dry-run mode to inspect the endpoint, recipients, subject, and body before every important send.
Use unique files with restrictive permissions and remove them after delivery.
Confirm recipients and the trusted Recoup endpoint before sending sensitive content.
anti_patterns: Do not build email payloads with shell interpolation or inline JSON quoting.
Do not pass secrets, unrelated local files, or unapproved recipient addresses.
Do not report success when the helper returns a nonzero exit code.

faq.question: Which message formats are supported?
faq.answer: The helper supports HTML and plain-text bodies supplied directly or read from local files.

faq.question: Can I preview an email without sending it?
faq.answer: Yes. Dry-run mode validates the body and prints the target and serialized payload without making a network request.

faq.question: Which credentials are required?
faq.answer: Live sending requires RECOUP_API_KEY or RECOUP_ACCESS_TOKEN in the environment. Dry-run mode does not require either credential.

faq.question: What happens when no recipient is supplied?
faq.answer: The Recoup API defaults delivery to the account email associated with the credential.

faq.question: Does the helper prevent empty emails?
faq.answer: Yes. It exits with an error unless the HTML or plain-text body contains non-whitespace content.

faq.question: Does it support attachments or scheduled delivery?
faq.answer: No. The helper only sends HTML or plain-text messages with recipients, carbon copies, subjects, and optional chat identifiers.
